title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot Chat usage report for GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly describes per-user prompt counts and active days as broken down by app; Microsoft documents those as overall Copilot Chat totals, with app-specific last activity dates. The roadmap facts and concealment controls are supported, but the licensed-user scope also needs to acknowledge conflicting Microsoft documentation.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Usage reports hide usernames and display names by default.
claims.quote: By default, all reports hide user information such as usernames, display names, groups, and sites to help companies support local privacy laws.

claims.claim: The concealment control is in Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Select Org Settings. On the Services tab, select Reports. In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings updates tenant-level report settings through the beta Graph API.
claims.quote:
Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports.
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings

claims.claim: The request body property displayConcealedNames controls concealment, and false displays identifiable information.
claims.quote: displayConcealedNames | Boolean | If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information. This property represents a setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Required.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The concealment setting is tenant-wide and affects all usage reports, including the Copilot Chat per-user table.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports. To learn how to display this information in usage reports, see Show user, group, or site details in usage reports.

claims.claim: Global administrators can change the setting to display concealed information.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it.

claims.claim: The setting also applies to Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and usage reports in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and to the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The report is read-only and takes no action on users or agents.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot Chat usage report read only report actions users agents per app prompts active days. Read microsoft-copilot-usage and activity-reports; they describe insights, exports and recommendation cards, not a read-only guarantee.
claims.fix: Replace the read-only/no-action assertions with 'The report provides insights into active usage of Microsoft Copilot Chat', as https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/activity-reports/microsoft-copilot-usage states. Remove 'only' from the risk rationale's description of reading usage counts.

claims.claim: The per-user table lists prompts submitted per app.
claims.quote: Prompts submitted | The total number of prompts submitted by this user to Microsoft Copilot Chat during the specified period.
claims.fix: Replace the first Data exposure bullet's opening sentence with 'The per-user table lists total prompts submitted and active days for Copilot Chat, plus overall and app-specific last activity dates.' The table at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/activity-reports/microsoft-copilot-usage gives app-specific dates, not app-specific prompt counts.

claims.claim: The per-user table lists active days per app.
claims.quote: Active days | The total number of days the user submitted prompts to Microsoft Copilot Chat within the specified timeframe.
claims.fix: Use 'The per-user table lists total prompts submitted and active days for Copilot Chat, plus overall and app-specific last activity dates.' See https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/activity-reports/microsoft-copilot-usage; active days are not defined per app.
